about: Refusals the host writes for a program that several packages recognise equally well, each held to the tie it comes from. The host's own case (the worker's `each_tie_is_worded_as_the_fixture_says`) builds each tie and holds the refusal the host writes for it to the text here, and holds `one_publisher` to the host's publisher test; the page's cases take these texts as the refusal a host reports. A change of the host's words turns the host's case red until this file says the new words.

two_publishers.refusal: it was not launched through the integration, and acme/codex (>=1.0.0, <2.0.0) covers version 1.4.0 and openai/codex (>=1.0.0, <2.0.0) covers version 1.4.0, and they come from different publishers or repositories, so neither is preferred, so no package was chosen for it and none of its bridges is admitted

three_publishers.refusal: it was not launched through the integration, and acme/codex (>=1.0.0, <2.0.0) covers version 1.4.0, openai/codex (>=1.0.0, <2.0.0) covers version 1.4.0 and other/codex (>=1.0.0, <2.0.0) covers version 1.4.0, and they come from different publishers or repositories, so none is preferred, so no package was chosen for it and none of its bridges is admitted
